1.explanation:
All text fields in a KML feature flow through the generic XML parser and KML reader before being handed off to the style/text renderer. 

• src/ol/format/KML.js is responsible for extracting the <name> (and other text) elements from a KML document. It currently takes the raw node text, which in some parsing modes still contains XML-entity encodings like “'”.
• src/ol/format/XML.js implements the low-level XML parsing utilities (node traversals, text extraction). It does not normalize or decode XML entities beyond what the XML parser itself provides, so any remaining ' or other named entities stay in the string.
• src/ol/format/XMLFeature.js wires up the XML parsing logic and maps element values into feature properties. It passes the un-decoded text along to the feature’s properties and ultimately into the style/Text pipeline.

Because the labels drawn on the canvas come straight from these parsed strings, the un-decoded entity shows up verbatim in the map. To fix the bug, one must add a decoding step (for example using a small entity-decode utility or calling DOMParser on the fragment) in the XML parsing path—ideally in XML.js or in the feature reader in KML.js—so that ' becomes ' before the text ever reaches the renderer.
1.bug_scenario: When loading placemarks from a KML file whose <name> element contains XML-escaped entities (in this case “Andy&apos;s”), OpenLayers renders the literal “'” in the canvas label instead of decoding it to an apostrophe. In the DOM caption below the map the entity is correctly resolved by the browser, but the map-drawing path shows the raw entity code.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/format/KML.js is responsible for reading the <name> and other text nodes from KML. It currently pulls nodeInnerHTML or raw nodeValue, preserving ' entities instead of returning decoded strings.
• src/ol/xml.js (the XML utility) provides the low-level functions for extracting textContent or nodeValue. If entity decoding isn’t happening here, the KML parser will see the raw entities.
• src/ol/style/Text.js takes the feature’s name property and passes it directly on to the renderer without any further decoding or sanitization of XML entities.
• src/ol/render/canvas/TextBuilder.js finally renders the text onto the canvas. Since it draws the string literally, any remaining &apos; sequences appear verbatim on the map.
Together, these files form the path from parsing the KML through to drawing the label. The fix is to introduce entity decoding (e.g. via a decodeHTML or decodeURIComponent step) in either the parser (in xml.js or KML.js) or at the start of the Text style (in Text.js) so that ' becomes ’ before rendering.
2.bug_scenario: When loading a KML file whose <name> is “Andy's”, the map displays the literal entity text “Andy&apos;s” instead of the decoded apostrophe “Andy’s”. In the example, the piepline is: the KML parser reads the XML, hands the raw string including ' through to the Feature properties, then the Text style and canvas renderer draw it without decoding HTML/XML entities.
